title: Basic Pentesting
summary: Service, web, and SMB enumeration led to credential discovery and Linux privilege escalation.
objective: Gain access to the target machine and retrieve the final password by chaining exposed services, weak credentials, and Linux permission issues.
pathSummary: Nmap identified SSH, HTTP, SMB, AJP, and Tomcat-related services. Web and SMB enumeration exposed usernames and notes, enabling an SSH password attack and later SSH key passphrase cracking for privilege escalation.
findings: Exposed development directory leaked enumeration hints.
Anonymous SMB access disclosed staff information.
Weak SSH credentials and readable SSH key material enabled account takeover.
lessons: Combine automated scanning with manual review.
Audit anonymous SMB shares and exposed development files.
Protect SSH keys and use strong passphrases.
mitigation: Disable anonymous SMB where unnecessary, remove exposed development notes, enforce strong authentication, and restrict private key permissions.

title: RootMe
summary: Web enumeration found an upload panel, leading to reverse shell access and SUID-based Linux privilege escalation.
objective: Gain initial access through the web server, retrieve the user flag, escalate privileges to root, and capture the root flag.
pathSummary: Gobuster discovered upload and file serving paths. A PHP reverse shell with an alternate extension bypassed filtering, and SUID enumeration found Python 2.7 as the root escalation path.
findings: Upload filtering allowed executable PHP payloads.
Uploaded content was reachable through the web server.
A SUID Python binary enabled root shell execution.
lessons: Test upload workflows for extension bypasses.
Keep uploaded files outside web-executable paths.
Audit SUID binaries regularly.
mitigation: Use strict file allowlists, store uploads outside executable web roots, and remove unnecessary SUID permissions.

title: rsa_oracle
summary: RSA oracle behavior was abused with modulus recovery and blinding to recover a password and decrypt an OpenSSL-protected message.
objective: Exploit the bank's encryption oracle to recover the encrypted password, then decrypt the intercepted ciphertext message.
pathSummary: Known plaintext and ciphertext pairs recovered the RSA modulus with gcd. RSA blinding bypassed the oracle restriction, and the recovered password decrypted the OpenSSL salted ciphertext.
findings: The oracle exposed chosen plaintext and arbitrary ciphertext behavior.
Known plaintext pairs leaked the RSA modulus.
Textbook RSA malleability enabled a blinding attack.
lessons: RSA without padding is malleable.
Oracle restrictions must be threat modeled against transformed ciphertexts.
OpenSSL salted files can be recognized from their header.
mitigation: Avoid unrestricted RSA oracles, use OAEP for RSA encryption, and use authenticated encryption for protected file contents.

title: Packets Primer
summary: A packet capture was searched for a plaintext picoCTF flag pattern using a binary-safe helper alias.
objective: Download the provided packet capture and analyze the captured traffic to recover the hidden picoCTF flag.
pathSummary: The capture was preserved as the original artifact and searched directly with the local picog helper. The binary-safe grep found the standard picoCTF flag pattern in the packet data, and Wireshark or tshark can verify the matching packet stream.
findings: The artifact was a packet capture with readable payload data.
The flag appeared directly in plaintext inside the capture bytes.
picog recovered the flag by matching the standard picoCTF flag format.
lessons: Start packet challenges with quick plaintext and flag-format checks.
Use binary-safe search when scanning captures directly.
Verify shortcut results with packet or stream context.
mitigation: Avoid transmitting secrets in plaintext protocols, encrypt sensitive data in transit, and review packet captures before public release.

title: sleuthkit intro
summary: A compressed disk image was extracted and analyzed with Sleuth Kit to identify the Linux partition sector count.
objective: Download the disk image, identify the size of the Linux partition using mmls, and submit the value to the checker service.
pathSummary: File inspection confirmed a gzip-compressed disk image. After extraction, mmls revealed the MBR partition layout and the Linux partition size.
findings: The artifact was a compressed raw disk image.
The disk used an MBR partition scheme.
mmls exposed the exact Linux partition sector count.
lessons: Verify file type before analysis.
Use partition analysis tools for disk images.
Record sector counts exactly when challenges depend on them.
mitigation: Sanitize distributed disk images and validate release files for unintended embedded information.

title: sleuthkit-apprentice
summary: Partition analysis and filesystem listing located a hidden flag file, which was extracted by inode from a forensic disk image.
objective: Recover the hidden flag from the provided forensic disk image.
pathSummary: mmls identified multiple partitions. Recursive fls searches found the target file in the second Linux partition, and icat extracted it by inode.
findings: The target file was stored in the second Linux partition.
Recursive filesystem listing exposed the useful inode.
icat recovered the file content directly by inode.
lessons: Analyze every partition in an image.
Use recursive file listing with focused filters.
Known inodes can speed up forensic extraction.
mitigation: Use secure wipe practices, full-disk encryption, and partition integrity checks to reduce recoverable sensitive data.

title: St3g0
summary: Image forensics and steganography tooling revealed hidden data concealed in a PNG artifact.
objective: Download the provided image file and identify the hidden flag concealed within it.
pathSummary: Metadata, embedded data, and steganographic channels were inspected with ExifTool, binwalk, and zsteg. LSB-based hidden content was identified and extracted.
findings: The PNG contained hidden embedded data.
binwalk identified compressed data indicators.
zsteg detected LSB steganography content.
lessons: Check metadata, file structure, embedded content, and steganographic channels.
Use multiple image forensic tools when a PNG appears suspicious.
LSB techniques are common in beginner steganography challenges.
mitigation: Remove unnecessary metadata and scan published media for hidden or embedded content.
